mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 1.0%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (p>0.05 for positive returns) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases (p>0.05 for negative returns) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 0.5% quarter-over-quarter and residential fixed investment (RSAFS) growth exceeds 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates a robust economy that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 0.5% qoq and RSAFS growth > 0.5% moq
failure_condition: When GDPC1 growth > 0.5% qoq and RSAFS growth > 0.5% moq, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (p>0.05 for positive returns) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), the strong labor market supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 4.0%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (p>0.05 for positive returns) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly growth rate in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% signals robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO growth > 0.5% moq, the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (p>0.05 for positive returns) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI growth rate above 3.0% signals persistent inflation, which may trigger monetary tightening and reduce equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL growth > 3.0% yoy, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases (p>0.05 for negative returns) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) both grow above 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates a robust economy in manufacturing and housing, supporting equity market performance and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth > 0.5% moq and HOUST growth > 0.5% moq
failure_condition: When INDPRO growth > 0.5% moq and HOUST growth > 0.5% moq, the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (p>0.05 for positive returns) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly growth rate in housing starts (HOUST) above 0.5% signals strong demand for housing and related sectors, supporting corporate earnings and equity market performance, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST growth > 0.5% moq, the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (p>0.05 for positive returns) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
